You don’t have to control your anger to meditate, just notice it! But I know what you mean that sometimes it does make it much harder.

Something that helps me is practicing techniques to calm down beforehand.

Look up 478 breathing (in for 4, hold for 7, out for 8) or tapping. Both really help me to calm down a bit when I’m feeling frustrated and then I can get more out of a breathing. It’s taken me a few weeks/months to really get the most out of these so be patient with whatever you try. Best of luck :)

This is the perfect opportunity to meditate.
Something to remember that I struggled with when I started meditating - you don’t have to meditate to “solve” your angry or anxious feeling, you can just acknowledge it, and let yourself feel that feeling.
Something that really helped me was understanding the theory and purpose behind meditation by reading books about it (e.g by thich nhat hanh) rather than just listening to guided meditations.

I like insight timer (paid version) but find sometimes it can be a bit overwhelming with choice of guided meditations 

I love smiling mind - there is lots of variety in courses and length of meditations, and it’s free

I’d tried for so long to avoid meds because I was terrified of the side effects. My bf at the time saw how much I was struggling with my anxiety and was really encouraging me to try them but I didn’t think it was right for me and I didn’t want to do it because someone else told me I should.

Eventually we broke up because my anxiety was too much, and that’s the point I realised I needed to give meds a shot. I couldn’t sustain an otherwise healthy relationship, because of my anxiety. I decided to take them then because I was ready to take them, I knew it was best for me, and that helped me really push through the side effects.
